maria: Quick config sanity-check — onboarding manifest for `starling-7b` shows:
```json
{
  "weights_uri": "gs://redwood-models/starling-7b/v1/weights.pt",
  "quantize": true,
  "quant_params": {"dtype": "int8"},
  "fallback_order": ["fp16","gptq-8bit","int8-llm"]
}
```
But runtime only supports `fp16` and `int8-llm` for the target arch; `gptq-8bit` will crash at load time. Also noticed tokenizer.json has `pad_token_id: null` which will blow up the tokenizer cast. Anyone seen this pattern before or should I patch the manifest?

tyler: I saw the config-lint CI fail earlier mentioning unsupported format `gptq-8bit`. We should add a validator to catch unsupported fallback entries per `target_arch`. Quick fix: reject unknown entries in `fallback_order`.

ash: For the tokenizer: if `pad_token_id` is null, the runtime tries to cast to int and fails during preprocessing. Short term: set `pad_token_id` to 0 in manifest defaults. Long term: schema must forbid `null` for numeric token ids or coerce them.

pranav: I'll open a tiny PR under `tools/config-schema` to add `supported_quant_formats` + unit test that runs sample manifests against each `target_arch`. Assigning to @tyler for review. Will include a test manifest that mirrors this one. PR #4523

ci-bot: config-lint: failed on branch feature/model-onboard — errors:
- unsupported_quant_format: gptq-8bit (module: validator/quant.py)
- tokenizer_pad_id_null: found null (module: validator/tokenizer.py)

maria: Thanks — i've updated the manifest to remove `gptq-8bit` from `fallback_order` and set `pad_token_id` -> 0. Pushed a tiny patch to the onboarding repo and added a note in the manifest about preferred order: `[int8-llm, fp16]`.

tyler: LGTM. When PR lands, can we add a quick smoke step in the onboard CI that runs `serve-config-check --target=runtime-x86` to catch these earlier?

pranav: yes. I'll add that to the PR plus a unit test that asserts the validator rejects unknown fallback entries.

maria: Done. Watching CI — if green i'll merge later today. :thumbsup:
